subject: naval-architecture
intro: Naval architecture leads to the people who design, build and operate ships and offshore structures — from hull lines and stability to the engine room and the offshore energy frontier.

roles.title: Marine Engineers and Naval Architects
roles.what: Design, develop and evaluate the operation of marine vessels, ship machinery and related equipment such as power supply and propulsion systems, for commercial ships, workboats and offshore assets.
roles.where: The course is the profession's curriculum: hydrostatics and stability with metacentres and load lines, hull forms and resistance, propellers and cavitation, hull girder strength in waves, and offshore platforms and marine renewables.

roles.title: Mechanical Engineers
roles.what: Plan and design tools, engines, machines and other mechanically functioning equipment, and oversee the installation, operation, maintenance and repair of engine and machinery systems.
roles.where: The marine propulsion unit — propellers, diesel and gas turbine plants and emerging fuels — is machinery engineering, and the fatigue and corrosion topics from ship structures decide how marine machinery survives at sea.

roles.title: Ship Engineers
roles.what: Supervise and coordinate the crew operating and maintaining engines, boilers, deck machinery and electrical, sanitary and refrigeration equipment aboard ship — the engine-room side of a merchant mariner credential.
roles.where: Marine propulsion's diesel and gas turbine plants and emerging fuels, plus the ship structures unit's corrosion at sea, are the systems a ship engineer keeps running on watch at sea.

roles.title: Engineering Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach university courses applying physical laws and engineering principles to machines, materials, processes and services — naval architecture and ocean engineering included — usually alongside research.
roles.where: Hydrostatics and stability, hull resistance and model testing, and wave loads on hull girders are exactly the lecture-and-laboratory content of a university naval architecture or ocean engineering department.
